messages:
kira: quick q — UX for the cost dashboard: should we surface prefetch/cache credits as a separate line item or just amortize them into per-token cost? thinking about canary routing + sticky routing making the attribution weird

matt: separate by default. engineers need to see where savings come from when debugging regressions. collapsed by default in the UI works well :thumbsup:

alyssa: separate + collapsed too. also show a per-request breakdown panel when you click a row (kv hit / prefetch / net compute tokens). most people won't expand so default stays simple

samir: agree. small note: telemetry volume explodes if we log every token-level event. add sampling + batch-aggregate keys: prefetch_id, route_id, model_sku. that gives us lineage without blowing up storage

kira: +1 on sampling. quick draft of the telemetry shape I sketched (conceptual):

```json
{ "event":"token_emit", "ts":1680000000, "model":"redwood-7b-q4", "route":"chat-transaction", "routing_reason":"primary", "cache_hit":false, "prefetch_id":null, "cost_microtokens":120 }
```

will add `prefetch_credit` bool and `prefetch_origin` enum (scheduled|on-demand) so we can split credits later

dina: finance asks: if prefetch benefits many tenants, how do we credit/cost-split? they want invoice-level determinism. my suggestion: attribute prefetch to the route that requested it originally, then expose a "shared benefit" view that estimates downstream tenant impact (informational only, not billable)

matt: that sounds reasonable. for billable fields keep deterministic rules: origin route gets the credit. show a projected savings column that spreads benefit across consumers (sampled estimate) — label clearly as estimated

kira: UX notes:
- dashboard row: route, model_sku, net_tokens, prefetch_tokens, kv_hits, estimated_prefetch_savings
- sparkline: show net tokens split area chart (compute vs prefetch vs kv). hover shows absolute numbers and sampling rate used
- drill panel: raw sampled events, prefetch lineage (prefetch_id -> list of consumer route_ids)

alyssa: can we add a toggle for canary views? i.e., show canary vs baseline token economics side-by-side for last 24h. helps teams decide if model swap is worth it

samir: backend implications: we need a compact proto for sampled token events and a windowed aggregator job to produce the per-route rollups. plan: sample at 1% by default, with adaptive sampling for high-cost routes to 5-10%

ops-bot: econ-ui v0.9 preview deployed to staging: https://staging.redwood/econ-ui/sparkline-probe - contains mocked prefetch columns

kira: next steps / owners:
- matt: prototype sparkline + hover (mock data) — due EOW
- samir: add sampling + compact proto in ingestion pipeline, include prefetch_id field — due next Wed
- dina: sync with finance on deterministic crediting rules and legal on labeling — due Tue
- alyssa: canary toggle UX mock + copy for estimated vs billable — due EOW
- kira: update telemetry spec in repo and add a small end-to-end demo using a seeded prefetch dataset

matt: noted. I'll push a prototype branch and link it in this thread when ready

dina: thanks — I'll pull finance in and share their constraints here

kira: cool. if nobody objects we'll roll the staging preview to a small set of power users next week to validate assumptions

samir: one more question — how do we tag prefetch_id for shared on-prem deployments where we can't leak tenant ids? plan: prefetch_id should be opaque and only map to tenant-agnostic route_ids in telemetry; full lineage kept only in private deployments

alyssa: makes sense. UX will avoid showing tenant lists for shared deployments and only surface aggregated impact

matt: branching off that, add feature flag `econ_show_prefetch_breakdown` so we can gate rollout

kira: agreed. thanks all — will follow up with PRs and the spec doc
